title: Analytical results of Typical Medium Theory for the Bethe lattice with Cauchy disorder
authors: A. Östlin, I. Titvinidze, M. Kollar, D. Jones, L. Chioncel
abstract: We present a combined numerical and analytically tractable realization of the typical medium theory (TMT) for Anderson localization on the infinite-connectivity Bethe lattice with Cauchy-distributed on-site disorder. Exploiting the special properties of the Cauchy distribution and the Bethe lattice, we derive an analytical expression for the typical density of states (TDOS) and obtain a simplified TMT self-consistency scheme. We show that the TDOS at the band center decreases linearly with disorder strength and vanishes at the critical disorder $W_c=D/2$. The resulting $ω$--$W$ phase diagram reveals the continuous collapse of the mobility edge and the disappearance of extended states.
summary: This paper develops an analytical framework using Typical Medium Theory (TMT) to study Anderson localization on the Bethe lattice with Cauchy disorder. The authors derive key results showing that the typical density of states vanishes linearly at a critical disorder strength, signaling the continuous collapse of extended electronic states. This work provides quantitative insights into the metal-insulator transition in highly disordered quantum systems.
main_problem: The study aims to characterize the Anderson localization transition (metal-insulator transition) in a disordered quantum system.
main_result: The typical density of states at the band center decreases linearly with disorder strength and vanishes at a critical disorder $W_c = D/2$, indicating continuous collapse of extended states.
method: The authors employ Typical Medium Theory (TMT), which uses the geometric average of local quantities, to analyze the Anderson Hamiltonian on an infinite-connectivity Bethe lattice.
model_or_system: The system is non-interacting spin-less fermions hopping on a Bethe lattice subjected to random on-site energies drawn from a Cauchy distribution. The model is described by an Anderson Hamiltonian.
key_observables: Typical Density of States ($ho_{W}^{	ext{typ}}(\omega)$), Mobility Edge ($\omega_c$), Number of Extended/Localized States ($N_{W}^{	ext{ext}}, N_{W}^{	ext{loc}}$).
main_assumptions: The primary approximation is the use of Typical Medium Theory (TMT) over the conventional CPA, and analytical derivations rely on specific algebraic simplifications afforded by the Cauchy distribution.
figures_summary: Figure 1 numerically shows the typical density of states ($ho_{W}^{	ext{typ}}$) for varying disorder strengths, illustrating its suppression and the shrinking energy interval.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the TMT self-consistency loop for this specific system. It derives analytical expressions for key observables like $ho_{W}^{	ext{typ}}(0)$ and $\omega_c$, analyzing the continuous transition from extended to localized states, and deriving approximate forms for the imaginary part of the self-energy ($\Sigma_I$).
why_interesting: The rigorous application of TMT to characterize localization transitions provides powerful analytical tools applicable to understanding spectral properties in disordered quantum materials.

The blue curve with symbols corresponds to the DOS of the clean Bethe lattice. The half-bandwidth is D = 0.5.
Figure 2. TDOS ρW typ(ω) at ω = 0 as a function of the disorder strength W. The orange dashed line shows the analytical result.

Figure 4. ω–W phase diagram for the Bethe lattice with Cauchy-distributed disorder. The green curve denotes the mobility edge separating the metallic and localized (insulating) phases. The color map shows the TDOS ρW typ(ω).

Figure 3. Mobility edge ωc as a function of the disorder strength W for the Bethe lattice with Cauchy-distributed disorder. For |ω| > ωc, the TDOS vanishes, ρW typ(ω) = 0. The dotted red line corresponds to a fit obtained from Eq. (8), with the fitting parameters a = 0.6874.

Figure 5. Number of extended and localized states, N W ext and N W loc, as a function of the disorder strength W for the Bethe lattice with Cauchy-distributed disorder. Results are shown at three fillings: half-filling (solid lines), Ntot = 0.4 (dashed lines), and Ntot = 0.2 (dash-dotted lines). The color coding of the curves is given in the legend.
